clue.text: Study oneself in awfully rotten pics

indicators.note: something done awfully is done badly, so the letters that follow come out in a garbled order

blocks.note: taken as written, ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone examines themselves after seeing some dreadful photographs.
explanation.definitionFit: To introspect is to look inward and examine your own thoughts and feelings, a kind of self-study.

clue.text: State broadcast supports Islamic leader

indicators.note: a leader goes at the front, so only the opening letter of the word is kept
in a down entry, a piece that supports another sits beneath it

blocks.note: the first letter of Islamic
a programme that was broadcast ran on air

explanation.surface: Government television backs a religious head of state.
explanation.definitionFit: Iran is a country, and a state can mean a sovereign nation.

clue.text: Passage from feature about northern society

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word wraps around the following letters

blocks.note: a trait is a characteristic feature
N is the abbreviation for northern
S is the abbreviation for society

explanation.surface: An excerpt taken from a magazine article about a club in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: N and S go inside TRAIT after its first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Transit is the act of going through or across, the journey of passage from one place to another.

clue.text: Rising ancient heroes crushed

indicators.note: something crushed is smashed out of shape, so the letters lose their order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Legendary warriors of old are defeated.
explanation.definitionFit: Something increasing is going up in number or amount, which is what rising means here.

clue.text: One won’t fight treaty (provided one’s involved)

indicators.note: being involved means being caught up inside, so these pieces go within the word for treaty

blocks.note: a pact is a treaty
provided can mean on condition that, i.e. if
I is the Roman numeral one, and the apostrophe s stands for is

explanation.surface: A conscientious objector declines to sign a peace agreement, conditional though it is.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket reads as a legal caveat, but it carries the wordplay; the apostrophe s in one's stands for is.
explanation.definitionFit: A pacifist is opposed to war and violence, so refuses to take up arms.

clue.text: Bit of gear I hung around head of Ronnie Barker?

indicators.note: hanging around something means surrounding it, so the earlier pieces enclose the next letter
the head is the top, so only the opening letter of the name is used

blocks.note: a cog is a tooth on a gearwheel
taken as written
the first letter of Ronnie

explanation.surface: A comedy prop from the British comic Ronnie Barker, star of The Two Ronnies.
explanation.walkthrough: Ronnie Barker was a British comedian, which makes the final word look like his surname rather than a definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A corgi is a small dog, and dogs bark, so this is an example of an animal that yaps; the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: Pretty person picked up in Hackney, I’m told

indicators.note: being told something means hearing it spoken, so the word is judged by sound rather than spelling

blocks.note: a hackney carriage is a taxi, and the passenger a taxi picks up is its fare

explanation.surface: Someone collects an attractive individual in the London borough of Hackney.
explanation.walkthrough: Hackney looks like the London borough; here it is a hackney carriage, the formal name for a London taxi.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair is an old-fashioned word for good-looking, as in a fair maiden.

clue.text: Foolish fiend regularly gate-crashes a function

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the word is taken
a gate-crasher forces their way inside an event, so these letters push into another word

blocks.note: taken as written
sine is a trigonometric function
the second and fourth letters of fiend

explanation.surface: A demon turns up uninvited at a party, which seems a silly idea.
explanation.walkthrough: Function looks like a social event to gate-crash, but it is the mathematical kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Asinine means donkey-like, hence extremely stupid or silly.

clue.text: Fish bait, of a certain sort

blocks.note: first meaning: a kippered fish that turns reddish when smoked
second meaning: a false lead used to lure attention away from the truth

explanation.surface: An angler's description of what goes on the hook.
explanation.walkthrough: Fish bait reads as one phrase about angling; split it, and each half is a separate meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A smoked kipper is literally this, and the term also names a misleading clue planted as a decoy in a mystery.

clue.text: A political group mostly in pieces

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter of the word is dropped

blocks.note: taken as written
a political party is an organised group

explanation.surface: A political faction that has largely fallen to bits.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has come apart is broken into separate bits rather than whole.

clue.text: Quality-assured bananas

blocks.note: first meaning: officially confirmed as meeting a standard
second meaning: crazy, formally declared insane by a doctor

explanation.surface: A label on fruit promising the bananas have passed inspection.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods are certified when officially approved, and a person certified has been formally declared mad, which is what slang bananas means.

clue.text: Rate wine soprano and I drunk “top”

indicators.note: someone drunk staggers about, so the letters reel into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
S is the abbreviation for soprano in music
taken as written

explanation.surface: A singer and the speaker assess a bottle, then pronounce it excellent after drinking it.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotes around top suggest a tasting verdict; it is a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A jumper is a top worn on the upper body, and this is a knitted pullover in a South Asian style.

clue.text: Defence? I’d resign with e-file lost

indicators.note: letters that are lost have strayed from their places, so they are put back in a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An office worker threatens to quit after an electronic file goes missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: the answer is one particular defence.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the line of German fortifications along the western border before and during the Second World War, a defensive barrier.

clue.text: Menu priced incorrectly could show this

definitions.text: Menu priced incorrectly could show this

indicators.note: done incorrectly means done wrongly, so the letters are set out in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A restaurant bill with wrong prices reveals poor judgement.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a wrongly priced menu could display rashness on someone's part.
explanation.definitionFit: Imprudence is a lack of care or good sense, which a careless pricing mistake would demonstrate.

clue.text: Amiability can ultimately grate in service

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the closing letter of the word is kept
in places the earlier pieces inside the word for service

blocks.note: Mass is a church service
a tin is a can
the end of grate

explanation.surface: Friendliness may eventually wear thin during a long church service.
explanation.walkthrough: Grate and can look like verbs about irritation; can is a noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: Being matey means being chummy and sociable, so the noun names a pleasant friendliness.

clue.text: Rush job, but one that lasts for years?

definitions.text: job, but one that lasts for years

blocks.note: first meaning: to hurtle along out of control

blocks.clueFragment: job, but one that lasts for years
blocks.note: second meaning: a lifelong profession rather than a single post

explanation.surface: A hurried piece of work contrasted with long-term employment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rush job' reads as a phrase for hasty work, but Rush stands alone as the first definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To career is to speed wildly, and the noun is someone's occupation pursued across a working life.

clue.text: Digs daughter with spirit entered into diaries

indicators.note: something entered into another is written inside it, so these letters go within the word for diaries

blocks.note: logs are diaries or records
D is the abbreviation for daughter
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: A daughter's notes on alcohol recorded in journals.
explanation.walkthrough: Digs is British slang for rented rooms, not a verb about excavating.
explanation.definitionFit: Digs and lodgings are both rented rooms where a person lives, usually in someone else's house.

clue.text: English maiden aboard river boat, say

indicators.note: being aboard means being carried within a vessel, so these letters sit inside others

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for river
Noah's ark is a boat
E is the abbreviation for English
M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: An English girl travels on a riverboat.
explanation.walkthrough: E and M go between R and ARK.
explanation.definitionFit: To remark is to comment or mention something, a close synonym of the verb in question.

clue.text: A thousand whales seen around popular island

indicators.note: being seen around something means surrounding it, so the earlier letters wrap the next word

blocks.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
the orca is the killer whale
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: Large numbers of whales spotted off a holiday island.
explanation.walkthrough: A thousand whales reads as a big pod; it splits into a Roman numeral and one kind of whale.
explanation.definitionFit: Minorca is one of the Balearic islands in the Mediterranean off Spain.

clue.text: H-pawns and knights, perhaps

blocks.note: H and horse are both slang for heroin
chess pieces are called men, and pawns are the humblest of them

explanation.surface: A chess commentary on pawns on the h-file and the knights beside them.
explanation.walkthrough: H-pawn is a real chess term, which hides that H stands alone for drug slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Mounted knights rode into battle, so they are one example of riders on steeds; perhaps marks the example.

clue.text: Ex-player squad held in stitch-up!

indicators.note: read as having held in, the word for squad keeps the next word inside it
in a down entry, up means the letters are read from bottom to top

blocks.note: a team is a squad
to sew is to stitch

explanation.surface: A former squad member is framed by teammates.
explanation.walkthrough: A stitch-up is British slang for a frame-up; here it splits into stitch plus a reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: This Hollywood actress is long dead, so she is a former performer; player can mean an actor.

clue.text: Preventive measures to avoid crowning?

blocks.note: surface reading: steps taken to stop someone being made monarch
setter's reading: a crown is a cap fitted over a decayed tooth, which good brushing and flossing make unnecessary

explanation.walkthrough: Crowning suggests a coronation; the setter means dental work.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping teeth clean prevents decay, so a dentist never needs to fit caps over damaged teeth.

clue.text: One that could raise army to protect India

indicators.note: protecting something means surrounding and shielding it, so one word wraps the other

blocks.note: a host is an archaic word for an army
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A recruiting call to muster soldiers to defend India.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoist is a lifting device such as a crane or winch, which lifts heavy loads.

clue.text: Short chaps getting son and husband fit together

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the last letter of the word is removed

blocks.note: chaps are men
S is the abbreviation for son
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: Small men watch their son and husband become healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Gears mesh when their teeth interlock, so the verb means to engage or interlock neatly.

clue.text: European wearing no pants

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the preceding letters are badly made and need rearranging

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A continental visitor going about without trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: Pants looks like underwear or trousers; as a British adjective it means poor or rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Norway is a native of a Scandinavian country on the continent.

clue.text: Those people taking English as subject

blocks.note: them refers to those people
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A group of students choosing English as their subject.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the topic or main idea a work deals with.

clue.text: Times leads with “Expect riots after secession”

indicators.note: leads are what go in front, so the opening letter of each following word is taken

blocks.note: the initial letters of the four words

explanation.surface: A newspaper headline predicting unrest once a region breaks away.
explanation.walkthrough: Times looks like the newspaper running the headline; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Eras are periods of history, and times in the plural can mean ages or epochs.

clue.text: The star act juggled with difficulty

indicators.note: things that are juggled are tossed about and land in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The headline performer struggled to keep the balls in the air.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something at a stretch means managing it only by straining, barely and with effort.
